letterText:
My dear colleagues,

Forgive me — this dispatch reaches you at a most ungentlemanly hour, the notice scandalously short, and for that breach of soldierly courtesy I beg your pardon before all else.

A matter has arisen, sudden and unbidden, of the sort a man can neither foresee nor in good conscience turn aside from. I am thus compelled to strike my tent and absent myself from the line upon Thursday and Friday both, answering the muster on neither day.

Hold the works in my stead, I pray you, and think not ill of me. I shall return to my post when these two days are spent.

I remain — though called suddenly away, and sick at heart to leave you short-handed — devoted still to the cause.
dateLine: From the Encampment, this 30th day of June
title: A Letter from the Front
